articles.title: Chamari Athapaththu’s 83 sinks Pakistan as Sri Lanka chase down 178 target to reach Asian Games final
articles.summary: Cricket News: Sri Lanka Women stormed into the gold-medal match of the Asian Games 2026 women’s cricket tournament after captain Chamari Athapaththu produced a matc.
articles.body: Sri Lanka Women stormed into the gold-medal match of the Asian Games 2026 women’s cricket tournament after captain Chamari Athapaththu produced a match-winning knock to guide her side to an eight-wicket victory over Pakistan in the first semi-final on Sunday.Chasing 178 at Korogi Sports Park, Sri Lanka reached 178/2 in 17.5 overs, sealing the win with 13 balls to spare. The victory guarantees Sri Lanka at least a silver medal, while Pakistan will compete in the bronze-medal match.Pakistan post competitive totalAfter a delayed start, Pakistan recovered from an early setback through a strong partnership between Ayesha Zafar and Shawaal Zulfiqar. Zafar led the charge with an aggressive 71 off 40 balls, while Zulfiqar contributed 54 off 50 deliveries. The pair added 115 runs to put Pakistan in a strong position before the team finished its 20 overs at 177/4.Athapaththu leads Sri Lanka’s emphatic chaseSri Lanka’s chase was anchored by Athapaththu, who struck an unbeaten 83 off 50 balls. Her innings featured seven boundaries and six sixes as she took control of the contest after settling in. Imesha Dulani added 26 off 21 balls, helping Sri Lanka maintain momentum, while the captain continued to attack the Pakistan bowlers and guide her team towards the target.Pakistan struggled to contain Sri Lanka, with their bowling and fielding unable to halt the scoring. Sri Lanka eventually completed the chase in 17.5 overs, losing just two wickets.The win sends Sri Lanka into the gold-medal match, where they will face the winner of the second semi-final between India and Bangladesh. Pakistan, meanwhile, will take on the losing side in the bronze-medal playoff.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Smriti Mandhana creates history in Asain Games semi-final, becomes leading run-scorer in Women's T20I
articles.summary: Cricket News: Smriti Mandhana made history in the Asian Games 2026 semi-final, becoming the highest run-scorer in women’s T20I cricket. The India opener achieved th.
articles.body: Smriti Mandhana made history in the Asian Games 2026 semi-final, becoming the highest run-scorer in women’s T20I cricket. The India opener achieved the milestones during a blistering start against Bangladesh, as India raced to 71/1 in the powerplay in their bid to book a place in the gold-medal match.India captain Harmanpreet Kaur won the toss and elected to bat first in the second semi-final. Mandhana and Shafali Verma provided an explosive start, putting Bangladesh’s bowlers under pressure from the outset.Mandhana surpasses Suzie BatesMandhana struck 37 off just 19 deliveries, hitting five fours and two sixes before her innings ended in the final over of the powerplay. She attempted another slog sweep off Nahida Akter but mistimed the shot, with Sobhana Mostary completing the catch at deep mid-wicket.Despite her dismissal, Mandhana had already etched her name in the record books, moving past New Zealand’s Suzie Bates to become the leading run-scorer in women’s T20Is. She also became the first Indian woman to reach 100 sixes in the format.Most runs in Women’s T20IsPlayerRunsSmriti Mandhana4,788Suzie Bates4,758Harmanpreet Kaur4,287Chamari Athapaththu4,282Sophie Devine3,817India make a flying startShafali joined Mandhana in attacking Bangladesh’s bowling, helping India reach 71/1 in the first six overs. The opening stand gave India early momentum in a high-stakes contest, with a place in the gold-medal match on the line.Playing XIs for India Women vs Bangladesh Women in the Asain Games Semi-finalIndia Women: Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Gunalan Kamalini, Harmanpreet Kaur (c), Richa Ghosh (wk), Bharti Fulmali, Deepti Sharma, Shreyanka Patil, Shree Charani, Nandani Sharma, Kranti Gaud.Bangladesh Women: Dilara Akter, Juairiya Ferdous, Sobhana Mostary, Nigar Sultana (wk/c), Shorna Akter, Sharmin Akhter, Shanjida Akter Meghla, Rabeya Khan, Nahida Akter, Marufa Akter, Sultana Khatun.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
